literal: Hong's son Jie, styled Yongshou.
idiomatic: Hong's son Jie, styled Yongshou.

literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the privilege of the same rites as the Three Dukes and Duke of Lecheng.
idiomatic: In Yuanxiang he was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Three-Duke rites and Duke of Lecheng.

literal: Hong's younger brother Zun held Administrator of Lintao.
idiomatic: Younger brother Zun was Lintao Administrator.

literal: At death posthumous name Si.
idiomatic: At death posthumous name Si.

literal: Zun's younger brother Rong held Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.
idiomatic: Younger brother Rong was Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.

literal: His son Xiong, styled Xiuwu, in youth was brave and decisive, light with wealth and heavy with spirit.
idiomatic: Son Xiong, styled Xiuwu, was young, brave, light with wealth, heavy with spirit.

literal: He held Inspector of Yan and Baron of Pingcheng.
idiomatic: He was Yan Inspector and Baron of Pingcheng.

literal: Following Erzhu Zhao in battle with Qi Shenwu, defeated at Guang'a, he led his command and held Dingzhou, submitting to Shenwu.
idiomatic: Following Erzhu Zhao against Qi Shenwu, beaten at Guang'a, he held Dingzhou and submitted to Shenwu.

literal: His older cousin Jie was Zhao's Cangzhou inspector; he also sent envoys to surrender.
idiomatic: Cousin Jie was Zhao's Cangzhou inspector; he too sent envoys to surrender.

literal: Shenwu, because the brothers both showed sincere intent, had Jie act as acting Yingzhou affairs.
idiomatic: Shenwu, seeing sincere intent in both brothers, had Jie act for Ying.

literal: He had Xiong replace Jie as Ying Inspector and advanced his rank to duke.
idiomatic: He made Xiong replace Jie as Ying Inspector and advanced him to duke.

literal: At the time the prohibition net was loose; officials mutually amassed wealth.
idiomatic: The prohibition net was loose; officials amassed wealth together.

literal: Only Xiong took after righteousness; he treated subordinates with kindness and was much cherished by officials and people.
idiomatic: Only Xiong took after righteousness; he treated subordinates kindly and was cherished.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei entered the Pass, Xiong was Grand Commander.
idiomatic: When Wei Xiaowu entered the Pass, Xiong was Grand Commander.

literal: Following Gao Anguo he broke Heba Sheng at Rangcheng and was then made Inspector of Yu.
idiomatic: Following Gao Anguo he broke Heba Sheng at Rang and was made Yu Inspector.

literal: Yuan Hongwei held Yingchuan in rebellion.
idiomatic: Yuan Hongwei rebelled holding Yingchuan.

literal: The rebel Zhao Jizong killed Yingchuan Administrator Shao Zhao, held Lekou, and answered Hongwei in the north.
idiomatic: Rebel Zhao Jizong killed Yingchuan Administrator Shao Zhao, held Lekou, and answered Hongwei from the north.

literal: Xiong attacked; Jizong was defeated and fled.
idiomatic: Xiong attacked; Jizong was beaten and fled.

literal: Within the city, because Xiong had gone out, they seized the province and called in Western Wei.
idiomatic: While Xiong was out the city seized the province and called in Western Wei.

literal: Xiong again with Mobile Secretariat Hou Jing pacified it.
idiomatic: Xiong again with Hou Jing pacified it.

literal: Liang generals Li Hongzhi and Wang Dangbo stormed and took Pingxiang; Xiong captured them both.
idiomatic: Liang generals Li Hongzhi and Wang Dangbo took Pingxiang; Xiong captured both.

literal: He also broke Liang Inspector of Si Chen Qingzhi and again besieged Southern Jing.
idiomatic: He broke Liang Si Inspector Chen Qingzhi and again besieged Southern Jing.

literal: Eastern rescue had not arrived; Xiong took the city.
idiomatic: Eastern rescue had not come; Xiong took the city.

literal: Liang made Yuan Qinghe Prince of Wei to harass the southern border.
idiomatic: Liang made Yuan Qinghe Prince of Wei to harass the south.

literal: Xiong greatly defeated him at Nandun.
idiomatic: Xiong greatly defeated him at Nandun.

literal: Soon he with Mobile Secretariat Hou Jing took Liang's Chucheng.
idiomatic: Soon with Hou Jing he took Liang's Chucheng.

literal: Men of Yu province memorialized, again asking for Xiong as inspector; he again conducted Yu affairs.
idiomatic: Yu men memorialized again for Xiong as inspector; he again ran Yu.

literal: Yingzhou Chief Administrator He Ruo seized Inspector Tian Xun, held the province, and surrendered to Western Wei.
idiomatic: Ying Chief Administrator He Ruo seized Inspector Tian Xun, held the province, and surrendered to Western Wei.

literal: The edict ordered Xiong with Guangzhou Inspector Zhao Yu and Yangzhou Inspector Shi Bao to follow Mobile Secretariat Ren Xiang in attacking.
idiomatic: The edict ordered Xiong with Zhao Yu of Guangzhou and Shi Bao of Yangzhou to follow Ren Xiang in attack.

literal: Western Wei general Yi Feng defeated Xiang and the rest; Yu and Bao each returned and held their cities, surrendering to the enemy.
idiomatic: Western Wei general Yi Feng beat Xiang; Yu and Bao returned to their cities and surrendered.

literal: Xiong gathered scattered troops and held Daliang.
idiomatic: Xiong gathered scattered troops and held Daliang.

literal: Zhou Emperor Wen sent his Vice Director Wei Xiaokuan and others to attack Yu; Xiong's commander Cheng Duobao surrendered.
idiomatic: Zhou Wen sent Vice Director Wei Xiaokuan to attack Yu; commander Cheng Duobao surrendered.

literal: They seized Inspector Feng Yong and with Xiong's household and subordinates' wives numbering thousands intended to send them to Chang'an.
idiomatic: They seized Inspector Feng Yong and Xiong's household and subordinates' wives by the thousands, bound for Chang'an.

literal: At Lekou, friend Outer Troops Staff Officer Wang Hengjia and commander Helian Jun and others intercepted from Daliang.
idiomatic: At Lekou, staff officer Wang Hengjia and commander Helian Jun intercepted from Daliang.

literal: They beheaded Duobao and brought Xiong's household back to Daliang.
idiomatic: They beheaded Duobao and brought Xiong's household back to Daliang.

literal: Xiong separately broke Lekou, captured Cheng Bo, and advanced to attack Xianhu.
idiomatic: Xiong separately broke Lekou, captured Cheng Bo, and advanced on Xianhu.

literal: Again Xiong was made acting Inspector of Yu.
idiomatic: Again he was acting Yu Inspector.

literal: Western Wei made Shi Bao Yangzhou inspector, holding Xiangcheng; Yi Inspector Han Xian held Nandun.
idiomatic: Western Wei made Shi Bao Yangzhou inspector at Xiangcheng; Yi Inspector Han Xian held Nandun.

literal: In one day Xiong took both cities, captured Xian and Chief Administrator Yue; Bao fled.
idiomatic: In one day he took both cities, captured Xian and Chief Administrator Yue; Bao fled.

literal: He was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the privilege of the same rites as the Three Dukes, still followed Hou Jing in pacifying Luoyang, and again was made Inspector of Yu.
idiomatic: He was Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Three-Duke rites, followed Hou Jing to pacify Luoyang, and again was Yu Inspector.

literal: Though Xiong was a martial man, his nature was generous and thick; in government he took only the great outline.
idiomatic: Though a martial man, Xiong was generous; in government he kept only the great outline.

literal: On the frontier ten years he repeatedly had merit.
idiomatic: Ten years on the frontier brought repeated merit.

literal: He loved people and gave much away; he was also praised for this.
idiomatic: He loved people and gave much away; he was praised for that too.

literal: In the fourth year of Xinghe he died at Ye; posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous name Wugong.
idiomatic: In Xinghe year four he died at Ye; posthumously Minister of Works, posthumous name Wugong.

literal: His son Shi inherited.
idiomatic: Son Shi inherited.

literal: Liu Chong, styled Sengsheng, was a man of Jie in Hedong.
idiomatic: Liu Chong, styled Sengsheng, came from Jie in Hedong.

literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Gui was Jin Director of Justice.
idiomatic: Seventh-generation ancestor Gui was Jin Director of Justice.

literal: Chong was refined and had capacity; eight feet tall, beautiful beard and bright eyes, and together had learning and conduct.
idiomatic: Chong was refined and capable, eight feet tall, fine beard and bright eyes, with learning and conduct.

literal: Presented as Outstanding Talent, he ranked high in the archery-and-policy examination.
idiomatic: Presented as Outstanding Talent, he ranked high in archery and policy.

literal: On leaving the sack he was Chief Clerk to the Grand Minister; transferred to Outer Troops Gentleman in the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: On leaving the sack he was Grand Minister Chief Clerk; transferred to Outer Troops Gentleman in the Masters of Writing.

literal: At the time Hedong and Hebei commanderies disputed the border.
idiomatic: Hedong and Hebei disputed the border.

literal: Between them were rich salt pools and the convenience of Yufan Pass; magistrates and common people all feared outside partition.
idiomatic: Between them lay rich salt pools and Yufan Pass; magistrates and people feared partition.

literal: Public and private factions competed; clamor filled the central offices.
idiomatic: Factions competed; clamor filled the central offices.

literal: Xiaowen therefore sent Chong to inspect and decide; above and below the lawsuits ceased.
idiomatic: Xiaowen sent Chong to inspect and decide; lawsuits ceased above and below.

literal: As Jing and Ying were newly submitted and southern bandits watched for trouble, Chong was again ordered with staff to plan with provinces and commanderies and add comfort and persuasion.
idiomatic: As Jing and Ying were newly submitted and southern bandits watched, Chong was again ordered with staff to plan with provinces and add comfort.

literal: On return he was made Mentor to the Heir Apparent and chief rectifier of his native commandery.
idiomatic: On return he was Heir Apparent Mentor and native commandery chief rectifier.

literal: He was promoted in succession to Administrator of Hezhong.
idiomatic: He rose in turn to Hezhong Administrator.

literal: When Chong first took the commandery, a man of the commandery named Zhang Ming lost a horse and suspected and seized more than ten people.
idiomatic: When Chong first took office, Zhang Ming lost a horse and seized more than ten suspects.

literal: Chong saw them, did not ask about the bandit affair, but to each separately gave a warm countenance and instead asked whether their parents and elders still lived and how much agriculture they had, while subtly observing their words and color.
idiomatic: Chong saw them, asked nothing of the theft, gave each a warm face, asked after parents and harvest, and watched their color.

literal: He immediately obtained the true bandits Lü Mu and two others; the rest were all released.
idiomatic: He at once had the true thieves, Lü Mu and one other; the rest were released.

literal: Within the commandery they submitted in awe; within the borders all was calm.
idiomatic: The commandery submitted in awe; the borders were calm.

literal: He died in office; posthumously made Inspector of Qi, posthumous name Mu.
idiomatic: He died in office; posthumously Qi Inspector, posthumous name Mu.

literal: Writings Chong composed were lost in the turmoil of invasion.
idiomatic: Writings he composed were lost in invasion.

literal: His eldest son Qinghe was by nature calm and did not compete in the age.
idiomatic: Eldest son Qinghe was calm and did not compete in the age.

literal: He held Palace Attendant and chief rectifier of his native commandery; he died.
idiomatic: He was Palace Attendant and native chief rectifier; he died.

literal: Qinghe's younger brother Kai, styled Shize.
idiomatic: Younger brother Kai, styled Shize.

literal: Eight feet tall, skilled in cursive script, he ranged fairly widely through literature and history.
idiomatic: Eight feet tall, skilled in cursive script, he ranged through literature and history.

literal: He held Marshal of the Pacification Army.
idiomatic: He was Marshal of the Pacification Army.

literal: Commentary: Qun Zun in learning knew the moment.
idiomatic: Commentary: Qun Zun's learning knew the turning of affairs.

literal: Heng then had measure to receive commission.
idiomatic: Heng had the measure to bear great trust.

literal: Zhang Pu and Gu Hun—civil and martial both used—their houses still shine through generations; is that not good?
idiomatic: Zhang Pu and Gu Hun, civil gift and martial both employed—their houses still shine through generations; is that not well?

literal: Gong Sunbiao at first was known from a single encounter; in the end he met blame through lightness.
idiomatic: Gong Sunbiao was first known from a single meeting; in the end lightness brought ruin.

literal: Gui first received the reward of probing gold; in the end he fell under suspicion of wealth—few keep their end to the end; it is not empty talk.
idiomatic: Gui first won the reward of gold probed from the vault; in the end he fell under wealth's suspicion—few keep their end; the proverb is not empty.

literal: Zhang Ji as envoy to the four directions had the beauty of extending reputation.
idiomatic: Zhang Ji, envoy to the four directions, had the gift of extending a man's name.

literal: Li Xian in learning and counsel was excellent and bore favor through three reigns.
idiomatic: Li Xian excelled in learning and counsel and bore favor through three reigns.

literal: Jia Yi early spread the reputation of the age.
idiomatic: Jia Yi early spread his name through the age.

literal: Xiu then did not fear the powerful.
idiomatic: Xiu then did not fear the powerful.

literal: Dou Jin and Li Xin—men of the time called them able pillars.
idiomatic: Dou Jin and Li Xin—men of the time called them able pillars of state.

literal: Jin for a phrase of suspicion, Xin for old grudge and suspicion—yet both met slaughter of the whole gate; truly pitiable.
idiomatic: Jin for a phrase held suspicious, Xin for an old grudge held in suspicion—yet both met slaughter of the whole gate; pitiable indeed.

literal: Han Yanzhi was loyal to what he served and had the fierceness of a champion of the state.
idiomatic: Han Yanzhi was loyal to his lord and had the fierceness of a champion of the state.

literal: Yuan Shi won meeting with Lord Cui and was heavy for breadth and elegance.
idiomatic: Yuan Shi won meeting with Lord Cui and was esteemed for breadth and elegance.

literal: Xiuzhi late showed sincere intent.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi in late years showed sincere intent.

literal: Tang He for ten thousand li admired righteousness.
idiomatic: Tang He, ten thousand li from home, admired righteousness.

literal: Kou Zan in sincerity and faith was praised.
idiomatic: Kou Zan in sincerity and faith won praise.

literal: Li Fan had wise vessels and reached through.
idiomatic: Li Fan had wise capacity and saw his way through.

literal: Daoyuan met his doom and had the spirit of one who sets his teeth in his beard.
idiomatic: Li Daoyuan met his doom with the spirit of a man who sets his teeth in his beard.

literal: Han Xiu in debating the frontier had the calculation to control the far.
idiomatic: Han Xiu, debating the frontier, had the calculation to hold the far.

literal: Yao Xuan by clever observation rose to rank; rites were added in life and death.
idiomatic: Yao Xuan rose by keen observation; rites followed him in life and death.

literal: Liu Chong's plain achievement had substance; vessel and conduct lasted through generations.
idiomatic: Liu Chong's plain learning had substance; character and conduct ran through generations.

literal: How magnificent!
idiomatic: Magnificent indeed!
